newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey agrees to experts meeting with Greece.
newsitem.headline: Turkey agrees to experts meeting with Greece.

text.p: Turkey accepted a European Union proposal on Friday calling for a meeting of Greek and Turkish experts this month to resolve differences between the two Balkan neighbours.
"The invitation to the meeting has been accepted by our side with pleasure," a statement from the Turkish foreign ministry said.
But Greek Foreign Minister Theodoros Pangalos said earlier on Friday that Greece would not send its experts to the meeting.

NATO allies Greece and Turkey agreed last month to each set up a committee of experts to discuss procedures on ways to tackle long-standing problems, including territorial feuds in the Aegean Sea separating the two countries.
The meeting, proposed by Dutch Foreign Minister Hans Van Mierlo, current head of the EU general affairs council, was to take place on May 26-28 in the Netherlands.

Pangalos has said Turkey must first renounce threats of war against Greece, talks should begin on accession of the divided island of Cyprus to the EU and territorial differences in the Aegean should be resolved in international courts.
Greece and Turkey came close to war last year over ownership of two uninhabited islets in the eastern Aegean.
Greece and Turkey have long been at odds over rights in the Aegean, Cyprus and a Moslem minority in northern Greece.
